50	\paragraph{Method-level interventions.} Three method-level strategies target different aspects of the independence bottleneck on Mistral-7B (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}). Independent Constraint Generation (ICG) bypasses trace-constraint coupling by generating constraints directly from the problem statement, but achieves only 74.6\% parse rate (vs.\ 97.1\% for trace-conditioned SICA; Appendix~\ref{app:constraint-quality}), reflecting limited standalone formalization capability at the 7B scale. ICG produces near-zero average effect ($\Delta = -1.96$\,pp and $+1.47$\,pp across two FOLIO seeds; $-0.50$\,pp on LogiQA; McNemar $p = .206$, n.s.). Paradoxically, among successfully parsed constraints, ICG produces objectively superior formulations: higher Z3 compilation (99.4\% vs.\ 96.5\%), lower redundancy (32.3\% vs.\ 42.9\%), and comparable discriminative rate (77.0\% vs.\ 81.4\%), yet yields no accuracy improvement across three seeds. This ICG paradox provides the most direct evidence that the bottleneck lies not in constraint quality per se but in the inescapability of same-model reasoning bias: independently generated constraints are cleaner and more diverse, but still encode the same model's systematic errors. Contrastive scoring generates pro and con constraints for each candidate but yields $\Delta = -9.31$\,pp on FOLIO ($p < 0.01$) and $-4.50$\,pp on LogiQA ($p = .160$, n.s.), with ${\sim}$21\% degenerate scores on both datasets; all 34 discordant questions produced non-degenerate scores (vs.\ 20.1\% degenerate in the full sample), indicating that scoring failures stem from systematic pro-bias rather than missing constraints; 62.7\% of Contrastive constraints are trivially satisfied by Z3 (Appendix~\ref{app:constraint-quality}), explaining the degeneration mechanism (Appendix~\ref{app:error-categorization}). Debate adds a proposer-critic-defense chain, producing $\Delta = -18.63$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.00$\,pp on LogiQA, both statistically significant by McNemar's test ($p < 0.001$ on both datasets). Discordant-pair analysis reveals the asymmetry: on FOLIO, 60 questions flipped from correct to wrong versus only 22 from wrong to correct; on LogiQA, 64 versus 18. Debate failures occur not when the debate process breaks down but when it succeeds: discordant questions average 2.93 effective debate rounds vs.\ 2.52 for concordant ones, suggesting that more extensive same-model debate produces more confident but incorrect constraints. Three of six method-dataset conditions reach significance, confirming that degradation is systematic, not stochastic. Only 15 of 79 unique discordant questions overlap between Debate and Contrastive (Jaccard $= 0.19$), confirming that the two methods attack different vulnerability types while sharing a common root cause in the independence bottleneck (Appendix~\ref{app:error-categorization}). At the 7B scale, multi-role prompting adds cognitive overhead that degrades both reasoning and extraction quality.

50	\paragraph{Method-level interventions.} Three method-level strategies target different aspects of the independence bottleneck on Mistral-7B (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}). Independent Constraint Generation (ICG) bypasses trace-constraint coupling by generating constraints directly from the problem statement, but achieves only 74.6\% parse rate (vs.\ 97.1\% for trace-conditioned SICA; Appendix~\ref{app:constraint-quality}), reflecting limited standalone formalization capability at the 7B scale. ICG produces near-zero average effect ($\Delta = -1.96$\,pp and $+1.47$\,pp across two FOLIO seeds; $-0.50$\,pp on LogiQA; McNemar $p = .206$, n.s.). Paradoxically, among successfully parsed constraints, ICG produces objectively superior formulations: higher Z3 compilation (99.4\% vs.\ 96.5\%), lower redundancy (32.3\% vs.\ 42.9\%), and comparable discriminative rate (77.0\% vs.\ 81.4\%), yet yields no accuracy improvement across three seeds. Moreover, ICG produces \emph{more} consistent outputs than trace-conditioned extraction: bootstrap-based constraint-set agreement yields $\kappa = 0.72$, exceeding the trace-level $\kappa = 0.44$ of standard SC. This suggests that model bias operates at the premise-understanding level, not merely at trace sampling---bypassing traces does not bypass the bias. The ICG paradox provides the most direct evidence that the bottleneck lies not in constraint quality per se but in the inescapability of same-model reasoning bias. Contrastive scoring generates pro and con constraints for each candidate but yields $\Delta = -9.31$\,pp on FOLIO ($p < 0.01$) and $-4.50$\,pp on LogiQA ($p = .160$, n.s.), with ${\sim}$21\% degenerate scores on both datasets; all 34 discordant questions produced non-degenerate scores (vs.\ 20.1\% degenerate in the full sample), indicating that scoring failures stem from systematic pro-bias rather than missing constraints; 62.7\% of Contrastive constraints are trivially satisfied by Z3 (Appendix~\ref{app:constraint-quality}), explaining the degeneration mechanism (Appendix~\ref{app:error-categorization}). Debate adds a proposer-critic-defense chain, producing $\Delta = -18.63$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.00$\,pp on LogiQA, both statistically significant by McNemar's test ($p < 0.001$ on both datasets). Discordant-pair analysis reveals the asymmetry: on FOLIO, 60 questions flipped from correct to wrong versus only 22 from wrong to correct; on LogiQA, 64 versus 18. Debate failures occur not when the debate process breaks down but when it succeeds: discordant questions average 2.93 effective debate rounds vs.\ 2.52 for concordant ones, suggesting that more extensive same-model debate produces more confident but incorrect constraints. Three of six method-dataset conditions reach significance, confirming that degradation is systematic, not stochastic. \section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.

\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}) constitutes the primary finding of this paper. SC ($\kappa = 0.44$), Diverse-Prompt ($\kappa = 0.40$), and ICG ($\kappa = 0.47$) cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$, forming a same-model ceiling: neither prompt variation nor independent constraint generation breaks the correlation. Debate reduces $\kappa$ to 0.15 (Eff-$K = 4.44$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. This independence-accuracy trade-off is a fundamental Pareto frontier: methods that increase trace independence necessarily degrade accuracy, while methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. Crucially, this trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results---DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}---each bypass same-model self-extraction, trading simplicity for architectures that introduce genuinely independent signal.

\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics applicable before any constraint extraction. First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: at Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical at $K = 12$), additional traces add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method.

\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} The only statistically significant effects in this study are negative. Among nine SICA conditions, none reaches $p < 0.05$ (best $p = 0.092$); the four-seed replication yields $p = 0.092$, $0.070$, $1.0$, and $1.0$. In contrast, SICA degrades significantly on ProofWriter ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p = 0.014$; $\Delta = -2.50$\,pp, $p = 0.011$). McNemar's paired test on method-level interventions sharpens this asymmetry: three of six method-dataset conditions reach significance (Debate $p < 0.001$ on both datasets; Contrastive $p < 0.01$ on FOLIO), all negative, with discordant pairs heavily skewed toward correct$\to$wrong flips. Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). This pattern---zero significant positives, multiple significant negatives---constitutes the strongest statistical argument for the independence bottleneck.

\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} The method-level interventions that test the trade-off most directly use Mistral-7B. At the 7B scale, Debate may impose cognitive overhead that larger models can absorb; whether 14B+ or 70B+ models shift the Pareto frontier is an open question. The trade-off itself is fundamental---it follows from the correlation structure of same-model outputs---but its severity may vary with scale. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.
